drafted_from: tool:put-back-what-runs's own row (its words, input schema and steps); read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run tool:put-back-what-runs with my declarations file." Find anything running that was changed by hand instead of from its rows, write it down, and put it back
no_lists_because: The owners and their things are a declarations file the person keeps; the findings are the answer (and a JSON-lines file with --findings), poured into a list by the caller.
instructions: 1. Write a declarations file: one row per owner, naming its module, its differences export, its put_back export, its interval_seconds and its things (for start-a-computer: module tools/start-a-computer/do-work/start-a-computer.mjs, differences hostLayoutDifferences, put_back applyHostLayout, each thing's args [machine, layout row]).
2. Say to your AI: "Run tool:put-back-what-runs", and give it declarations_file.
3. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:put-back-what-runs and its input (the worked example shows one).
4. Read what comes back: one finding row per difference, each saying whether it was put back.
